action: Check your NGINX and F5 NGINX products against F5 advisory K000164058. Update to version 1.31.9 once it is published. Until then, disable HTTP/2 on internet-exposed listeners to mitigate CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633.
date_note: Date of the CERT-SE notice; F5's own publish date was not read.
exec: NGINX sits in front of many web services; an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw there puts internet-facing systems at risk.
plain: Five serious flaws in the widely used NGINX web server could let an outsider run code on the server. A fixed version is not yet published; a temporary workaround exists.

key_findings: CERT-SE lists five CVEs, each with CVSS 8.1.
An unauthenticated attacker could execute code remotely with the privileges of the NGINX worker process.
CERT-SE says to update to version 1.31.9 as soon as possible once it is published; no release date is given.
For CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, CERT-SE advises disabling HTTP/2 on internet-exposed listeners.
recommendations: Disable HTTP/2 on internet-exposed listeners as an interim step for two of the CVEs.

summary: Sweden's CERT-SE warns of five serious NGINX vulnerabilities, each scored CVSS 8.1, that could let an unauthenticated attacker run code with the privileges of the NGINX worker process. It cites F5 advisory K000164058 and names many NGINX products as affected. CERT-SE gives no exploitation report and says the fix, version 1.31.9, is still to be published.
title: CERT-SE warns of five serious NGINX vulnerabilities allowing remote code execution

validation.note: CERT-SE notice read; the F5 advisory page did not load (needs a browser session). No exploitation reported, so severity 2.
